name: Week 19 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Lat Pulldown + Face Pull)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. **Warmup reminder:** behind-back shrug FIRST (protective activation, 3 sets) → band-pull-apart → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → active dead hang. Spotlights cycle forward to the lat pulldown (stepped to 150 on the regular machine W18 — 'clearly the new weight') and the face pull (stepped to 50 — 'hard even with good form'), drilling both at the new working numbers. W18's user-pulled steps are now the defaults: chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high cable curl 180. DB row holds the 70/80/90 bare-hand pyramid (grip the cap, no straps). Pull-up goes back to the straight bar — the swivel grip rotates toward the bicep and pulls work off the lats. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). Spotlights cycle to lat pulldown (now 150, regular machine) + face pull (now 50) — drilled at the new working numbers. New defaults from W18's user-pulled steps: chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high curl 180. DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps. Pull-up back to the straight bar. Both shoulders pain-free now ('only regular weakness') — grip is the cap, not the shoulder.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — stepped from 140 to 150 on the regular machine W18 ('140 was easy last week… clearly this is the new weight'), finished a bit ugly on the late sets. Spotlight drills the wide-grip, lats-to-the-back-pockets pull and the slow controlled return so 150 cleans up into solid reps — grip + back the honest cap, no straps.

Cycles forward — took the optional step to 50 W18 ('hard at 50 even with good form!') with the elbows still high. Spotlight drills the knuckles-up grip + elbows-above-the-shoulders cue that's the make-or-break for moving the work into the back, so 50 stays clean and the front shoulder never takes over.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly · W18 pull-up + DB row · W19 lat pulldown + face pull (current) · W20 cycle forward — high cable curl + cable crunch refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — the protective counter-movement to all the pulling can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**Pull-up back to the STRAIGHT BAR.** The adjustable swivel grip rotates toward the bicep mid-pull and pulls work off the lats (W18 self-discovery: 'probably not the best for pull ups'). Straight bar is the preferred variant — W18 held a clean 8/8/8/8 on it.

**Lat pulldown spotlight — 150 on the regular machine (back-left).** New working number; W18 it 'finished ugly / did too many,' so the reps will clean up as it settles. Per-equipment numbers below — pick what's free, log which.

**Face pull spotlight — 50, knuckles-up grip stays.** Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up, elbows ABOVE the shoulders — that's what unlocked 50 with the form holding. If the elbows drop, the front shoulder takes over — re-set them high.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set 90 felt good W18 ('could go up in reps') — let the reps creep on the 90 as the grip allows; grip is the limiter (left hand taps first), set the DB down when grip gives.
**High cable curl 180** — was 'easy on all sides, can go up' W18. A small further step (185-190) is earned IF it moves clean (you pull it); otherwise hold 180.

**Cable crunch — watch the magnetic micro add-ons.** The stack has add-on weights that can be on without you noticing (W18: a '67.5' was actually 70.5). Read the actual stack. 62.5 is the clean form-first base, 66.5 comfortable at x15, 70.5 the current brutal ceiling.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 45, reverse fly 20, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance; the left still struggles to hit 9-10 on the last incline-curl sets.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension. Primes the pull-ups.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched.

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8 (W18 held a clean 8/8/8/8).

**Back to the STRAIGHT BAR** — the adjustable swivel grip rotates toward the bicep mid-pull and pulls work off the lats ('probably not the best for pull ups'). The straight bar's been feeling best and keeps the work in the back.
- **Active hang start**, shoulders pulled down out of the ears — NOT a collapsed dead hang
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar — 'drive the elbows into the back pockets'
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping, no kip
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — frequency over max effort; both shoulders are pain-free now ('only regular weakness'), so grip + honest strength are the limiter, not the shoulder. Bank 6 clean over 8 sloppy.

sets.name: DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row + Chest-Supported Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — chest glued to the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze on the 70 and 80** — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, let the reps creep** — W18 was 90x6 and 'felt good, could go up in reps.' Drive the elbow, aim for clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. No straps — train the grip.

**LOAD:** 45 (the new working weight — stepped up from 40 W18, 'I guess this is my new working weight,' x12 all sets slow eccentric). 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides stay on the pad
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom.

**LOAD:**
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, ~2×10 on the bar; take the real preacher whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (default) — chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** — the left still struggles to hit 9-10 on the last two sets, so keep the left-first protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps ('getting hard at end, still good working weight' W18).
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop. Rear-delt / mid-trap shoulder-health work; quality over the number.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one + the number):**
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 150** (the new working number, back-left — stepped from 140 W18)
- **Dual pulley: 70**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean reps at the new 150:**
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — the honest cap, same as the DB row; no straps

**Reflection:** W18 the 150 'finished ugly / did too many' on the late sets — does it clean up this week (full reps, controlled return), or is 150 still grinding on set 3? The reps will tidy as it settles; bank clean reps over ugly ones.

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Column — Face Pull (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 50)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **50** (the new working number — stepped from 47.5 W18, 'hard at 50 even with good form!').

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — elbows high, work in the back:**
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 50 feel right with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop

**Reflection:** do the elbows stay above the shoulders for all 3 sets at 50, or do they drop and the front of the shoulder start taking over? Elbows high = the work's in the back. If they drop and stay dropped, that's the honest cap — back to 47.5 rather than grind 50 with low elbows.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): **180** — was 'easy on all sides, can go up' W18; optional **185-190 if it moves clean** (you pull this)
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start.

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one — AND read the actual stack):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — the clean form-first base; **66.5 comfortable at x15**, **70.5 the current brutal ceiling**
- **Watch the magnetic micro add-ons** — they can be on without you noticing (W18: a '67.5' was actually 70.5). Read the stack before you start.

3 sets.
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it. Only climb the load if the form holds; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free.
**Spotlight: lat pulldown + face pull.** Lat pulldown drills clean reps at the new 150 (regular machine); face pull drills the knuckles-up / elbows-high cue at the new 50.
**Pull-up back to the straight bar** — the swivel grip rotates to the bicep and pulls work off the lats. W18 held 8/8/8/8 clean on the straight bar.
**New defaults from W18's user-pulled steps:** chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high cable curl 180.
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Let the reps creep on the 90 ('could go up in reps' W18). Grip is the limiter (left hand).
**High cable curl 180** — optional 185-190 if it moves clean (you pull it); otherwise hold.
**Cable crunch — read the stack** (magnetic micro add-ons can be on unnoticed). 62.5 base, 66.5 comfortable, 70.5 ceiling.
**Loads otherwise hold** — reverse fly 20, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — the left still lags on the last incline-curl sets.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — both shoulders pain-free now ('only regular weakness'). No straps.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two lifts the user stepped up himself last week — the lat pulldown at the new 150 and the face pull at the new 50 — because clean reps at the new working number is how a fresh step settles in. Both shoulders are pain-free now, so grip is the honest cap on the heavy pulls (no straps), and the pull-up goes back to the straight bar to keep the work in the back. Loads otherwise hold; the floor rising is the win. Building decades, not weeks.
